item.title: Betting on Bots: A Deep Dive into Botnet Campaigns
item.description: As someone immersed in cybersecurity every day, botnets have always intrigued me with their evolving tactics and increasing sophistication, especially when they are Linux-based. Recently, I happened to come across some of the latest botnet campaigns. In our analysis, we explored how these bots are weaponized for distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks, malware distribution, and crypto mining operations. Additionally, we discussed how attackers are using increasingly automated techniques to monetize their botnets at scale.

item.title: An Elastic approach to large- scale dynamic malware analysis
item.description: In my work, I’m always looking for ways to scale malware analysis, and Elastic’s recent advancements really stand out. At Elastic Security Labs, we’ve been working on dynamic malware analysis at a large scale using our Detonate framework. The process involves running malware in sandboxed environments and analyzing behavior to extract meaningful insights. In our latest research, we explored techniques like enrichment pipelines, fingerprinting, and automation to handle massive datasets, filtering out noise and identifying malicious activity with precision.

item.title: NAPLISTENER: More Bad Dreams from the Developers of SIESTAGRAPH
item.description:
NAPLISTENER: More Bad Dreams from the Developers of SIESTAGRAPH

In recent research, we observed a shift in tactics from the threat group behind SIESTAGRAPH, focusing more on establishing persistent access rather than data theft. A new malware variant called NAPLISTENER, an HTTP listener written in C#, is designed to evade network-based detection. NAPLISTENER acts similarly to legitimate services, blending into the background by processing web requests and running commands in memory.

item.title: SUDDENICON Supply Chain Attack
item.description:
SUDDENICON Supply Chain Attack

In recent research, Elastic Security Labs analyzed the SUDDENICON malware, which targeted users of the 3CX VOIP software in a sophisticated supply-chain attack. The attack involved malicious DLLs embedded within the 3CXDesktopApp, which laid dormant for several days before initiating communication with command-and-control servers to download additional payloads. This attack highlights the growing trend of targeting software supply chains to compromise otherwise legitimate applications.

item.title: REF2924: How to Maintain Persistence as an Advanced Threat
item.description:
REF2924: How to Maintain Persistence as an Advanced Threat

In a recent update, we explored how the threat group behind SIESTAGRAPH, NAPLISTENER, and SOMNIRECORD maintains persistence in victim environments. Their toolkit includes custom malware, such as .NET webshells, and open-source tools like TFirewall and AdFind. These tools enable the attackers to blend into legitimate processes, establish footholds, and escalate privileges using scheduled tasks, DLL injections, and stealthy HTTP listeners.
